calls.head: Iron sharpens iron
calls.body: The Red Wings are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Panthers are one of the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Red Wings’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots. The Panthers take a lot of penalties and the Red Wings draw plenty of them, so their power play should get its chances.

calls.head: Markström gets another crack at the Red Wings
calls.body: Markström has been shaky against the Red Wings since 2023-24, well below his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if he looks like himself tonight.

calls.body: The Red Wings get in close, but the Panthers mostly shoot from distance. Detroit is near the top of the league for shots from in close, and Florida is near the bottom. Shots from in close tend to be more dangerous, so expect the Red Wings to do more of their damage around the net.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Red Wings beat the Panthers
paras: Carter Mazur, in his 18th NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Moritz Seider, early in the first to open the scoring for the Red Wings. Sam Reinhart made it 1-1 for Florida midway through the period, and Alex DeBrincat put the Red Wings back ahead 2-1 early in the second. Aaron Ekblad made it 2-2 for Florida shorthanded late in the period. The third period was a wild one. Justin Faulk and Michael Brandsegg-Nygård scored 45 seconds apart early in the period to put the Red Wings up 4-2. With the goalie pulled and less than four minutes left, Sam Bennett cut Detroit’s lead to 4-3. Emmitt Finnie shut the door with an empty-netter with just three seconds left.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. The Panthers hit five posts, and the bounces never came. Daniil Tarasov made 23 saves for the Red Wings, and Jacob Markström stopped 24 of 28 at the other end. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Andreas Englund, even without a point, by our Swing measure. The Red Wings improved to 7-5-3, still last in the Atlantic, while the Cats fell to 8-5-2, fifth in the Atlantic.

items.text: The Panthers’ three-game winning streak is over.
Alex DeBrincat extended his point streak against Florida to eight games.
Sam Reinhart has a point in four straight games, with a goal in each of the last three.
Aaron Ekblad scored his first goal of the season, his first since Mar 26 (15 games played since).
